what_it_does: This paper describes a battery-powered electronic nose—a tiny sensor system that detects diseases by analyzing chemicals in a person's breath. The core challenge is that sensor accuracy drifts over time and varies between different people, while conventional disease-detection systems either require constant cloud computation or draw too much power for portable devices. This work embeds a lightweight learning algorithm directly into the device's circuitry, consuming just 67 microwatts per channel. The chip continuously adapts to each patient's unique breath signature without needing an external computer, making diagnosis portable and personalized while staying battery-powered.
